summary: Australia requires almost every visitor to hold some form of authorization before boarding: Europeans apply for the free eVisitor (subclass 651), passport holders from the US, Canada, Japan and other ETA countries use the Australian ETA app (subclass 601, AUD 20 service charge), and everyone else applies online for a Visitor visa (subclass 600). New Zealanders are the exception — they receive a Special Category Visa automatically on arrival.

notes: Declare all food, animal products and plant material (including wooden articles), and any footwear, clothing and equipment used in rural areas or near animals. Australia's Department of Agriculture says a false or misleading declaration can bring an infringement notice of up to AUD 7,280, civil penalty proceedings or prosecution, and visa cancellation.

Duty-free alcohol: 2.25 litres of alcoholic beverages per traveller aged 18 or over, according to the Australian Border Force. Most tobacco products are prohibited imports, though travellers aged 18 or over may bring tobacco products in without a permit.
The Department of Agriculture asks travellers to make sure footwear and sporting and recreational equipment are clean and free from soil, seeds and grass.

safety.text: Canada's travel advice says violent crime is low, while petty crime occurs mostly in larger cities and vehicle break-ins are common. The main hazards the Canadian and UK governments describe are natural: rip currents at beaches, remote outback driving, and seasonal bushfires, floods and cyclones. Check local warnings.

tips.text: Declare every food item, plant product and wooden souvenir on your Incoming Passenger Card. Australia's Department of Agriculture says declared goods are inspected and returned if they pose no biosecurity risk, while a false or misleading declaration can bring an infringement notice of up to AUD 7,280 and cancellation of your visa.

Canada's travel advice says riptides are common on Australia's coast and several drownings occur each year: avoid unsupervised beaches, follow lifeguards' instructions and respect the beach flag warning system. The UK's says rip currents can happen at any beach.

Canada's travel advice says outback settlements are far apart and isolated: plan your overland route carefully, carry sufficient fuel, water and food, and take care driving in rural areas at night, when roaming animals and road trains are hazards.
The eVisitor is free on immi.homeaffairs.gov.au, and the ETA costs AUD 20 only in the official Australian ETA app. Third-party sites charging more for either are unnecessary middlemen.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Australia?
faq.answer: Yes — an electronic one. US passport holders must obtain the Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601) through the official Australian ETA app before boarding. It carries an AUD 20 service charge, is normally approved within minutes, and allows stays of up to 3 months per visit over 12 months.

faq.question: What is the difference between the eVisitor and the Australian ETA?
faq.answer: Both allow 3-month tourist or business visits over a 12-month validity. The eVisitor (subclass 651) is free and covers EU and other European passports, applied for on the Home Affairs website. The ETA (subclass 601) covers the US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, the UK and others, costs AUD 20 and is applied for only via the Australian ETA app.

faq.question: Do New Zealanders need a visa for Australia?
faq.answer: No application is needed. New Zealand citizens receive the Special Category Visa (subclass 444) automatically when they arrive, which lets them visit, live and work in Australia for as long as they remain NZ citizens.

faq.question: Can I bring food into Australia?
faq.answer: Only if you declare it. All food, plant material and animal products must be declared on the Incoming Passenger Card. Australia's Department of Agriculture says declared goods are inspected and may be treated, exported or destroyed, and those that pose no biosecurity risk are returned; a false or misleading declaration can bring an infringement notice of up to AUD 7,280, civil penalties or prosecution, and visa cancellation.

faq.question: Can I stay in Australia longer than 3 months as a tourist?
faq.answer: Not on an eVisitor or ETA — each visit is capped at 3 months. For longer trips, apply online for a Visitor visa (subclass 600), which can be granted for stays of 6 or even 12 months, before you travel or before your current stay expires.
